svg.text: always same length regardless of input
1. Deterministic: same input -> same hash always
2. Fast: quick to compute for any input size
3. One-way: cannot reverse hash to input (pre-image)
5. Collision-resistant: hard to find two inputs
with the same hash (second pre-image resistance)
Forensics: hash proves file integrity (tamper detection)
~50% of bits differ despite tiny input change.
Impossible to "nudge" a hash toward a target.
Receiver: Hash(received doc) == Decrypt(signature, public key) ?
YES -> document is authentic and untampered
NO -> document modified in transit or wrong signer
Used in: code signing, SSL/TLS, SSH, PGP email, git commit signing
sha256sum file.iso | sha256sum --check # verify download integrity
• Hash evidence files immediately on acquisition
• Record hash in chain of custody documentation
• Re-hash before analysis: proves no tampering
• NSRL database: match hashes to known malware
• Hash matching: find identical files across drives
Court-admissible only if hash recorded at acquisition.
Use SHA-256 or better for new forensic work.
